about.title: San Rafael Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: San Rafael saw 5 traffic deaths alongside 286 injury collisions in the most recent recorded year, numbers that represent real families now navigating grief and unanswered questions. Corridors like US-101, 2nd Street, 3rd Street, and Lincoln Avenue see steady traffic, and crashes tend to cluster around Friday early evenings when commuters and weekend travelers overlap. If you've lost a spouse, partner, parent, or child in a collision here, California law gives certain surviving family members a path to pursue accountability through a wrongful death claim. This is separate from any criminal case that might follow a fatal crash, and it exists to address the financial and personal losses a family carries forward. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves, but we can connect you with an attorney in our network who handles these cases on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover something for your family. You focus on your family; we help you find someone to talk to about the next step.
commonInjuries: Lost income and financial support the person provided
Loss of companionship, guidance, and care
Loss of household services and shared responsibilities
Medical costs incurred before death, where applicable
Emotional and relational losses recognized under California law

whyChoose.title: What Marin County Families Should Know

items.title: Who Can File Matters
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to specific people, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, then extending to other dependents or heirs if none exist. An attorney can help identify who in your family qualifies to bring the claim.

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though claims against a government entity (such as a public roadway defect) require much faster notice. Waiting too long can close off options entirely.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California law recognizes not just funeral costs and lost financial support, but the loss of love, companionship, and guidance a family member provided. These non-economic losses are a real part of what a claim can address.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Typically a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have first standing. If none of those exist, other dependents or heirs may be eligible. An attorney can review your family's specific situation to confirm who qualifies.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case against the at-fault driver?
items.answer: No, they're separate. A criminal case is brought by the state and focuses on punishment, while a wrongful death claim is a civil matter brought by the family to address financial and personal losses. One can proceed without the other.

items.question: Does it matter that the crash happened on US-101 or a city street like 2nd Street in San Rafael?
items.answer: The location can affect which agencies are involved and whether a government entity might share responsibility, which changes the filing deadline. An attorney can look at the specific road and circumstances to determine how that affects your case.

items.question: How much will it cost to speak with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing upfront. LawProactive is a free connection service, and attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if your family recovers compensation.
